description: Where T Third Street riders board: every public stop-, station- or segment-level figure found for the T Third (and its predecessors KT / 15-Third), Central Subway stations, 4th & King Caltrain-Muni transfers, and Chase Center/UCSF effects. Compiled to locate the beta3 model's shortfall (model ~7,900 vs SFMTA APC ~25,000-27,500 average weekday T boardings, 2025-10..2026-09). Numbers are copied exactly as published; anything computed here is in 'derived' and labeled as such.
bottomLine: No public 2024-2026 stop-level APC table for the T was found (SFMTA publishes route-level only; FTA lists no Central Subway Before-and-After study).

The newest station-level figure: SFMTA (via Mission Local, 2025-03-03) said 'not quite 9,500' board and 'not quite 12,700' alight per day at the Central Subway stations (the article says 'four', i.e. presumably incl. 4th & Brannan). T average weekday boardings that winter were 19,500 (Jan 2025) / 16,800 (Feb 2025, partial closure from Feb 26). So the Central Subway stations carried roughly half or more of all T boardings (derived ratio, see derived.centralSubwayShareEarly2025).

2023 faregate entries were much lower (about 1,250 + 1,110 + 350 = 2,710 weekday entries at the three underground stations), so Central Subway use grew several-fold 2023->2025, or the 2025 figure uses a different method (APC / exits); flagged uncertain.
Faregate exits exceed entries at the underground stations in both data points (Feb 2023: 4,501 vs 2,966; early 2025: 12,700 vs 9,500), so entries likely understate boardings there.
2024 peak-hour crowding (Muni Metro Capacity Study): Central Subway segment 15.0 sq ft/passenger, Mission Bay 18.7, Third Street South 26.2 -> peak loads highest north of 4th & King.

Latest public stop-level counts are 2006-07 (TEP ride checks, KT line, both directions): Third Street south of King St had 9,334 weekday boardings (Mission Bay 726, Dogpatch 1,908, Bayview+Visitacion Valley 6,700) plus 1,497 at 4th & King - already about 3x what the model now gives the same stops.

Caltrain transfer share at 4th & King specifically: not found. Systemwide Caltrain 2025 triennial: Muni is the access mode for 8% and egress mode for 5% of all Caltrain riders (all stations). The 2008 Central Subway SEIS forecast that 67% of 2030 passenger activity at the 4th & King T station would be Caltrain transfers (forecast, not observed).
